sections.h2: How Portland's layout shapes a sale
sections.html:
Where the Willamette meets the Columbia, Portland spreads across Multnomah County, with thin slivers extending into Clackamas and Washington counties. Street addresses use six sectors (North, Northeast, Northwest, Southeast, Southwest and South), and Burnside is the line between the northern and southern ones.

A house near Alberta or Hollywood in Northeast, one near Hawthorne or Belmont in Southeast, and one in St. Johns can sit within a short drive of each other yet attract very different buyers and very different repair lists.

The ground matters as well. The city is built over the Boring Lava Field, and a report from 2014 marked over 7,000 spots as high risk for landslides and soil liquefaction if a major quake hit. A hillside lot in the west hills and a flat lot east of the river come with different foundation, drainage and insurance questions.

Rain or snow measures on roughly 157 days each year, which makes damp the chief enemy of an old house. Long wet seasons are hard on roofing, gutters, siding and crawlspaces, and an inspector will study those first. Snowfall is small, about 4 inches, so snow load rarely ruins a roof.

Heat counts too: the record high is 116 degrees, set June 28, 2021, and about 61 days a year reach 80 or higher. Walk the roof line, gutters and any cooling system before you list.

The seismic and slope questions on the Oregon disclosure form carry extra weight in Portland because of the landslide and liquefaction mapping. Portland sits near the Portland Hills and East Bank faults. Answer every item truthfully, include whatever you know about retrofits or drainage work, and be ready for follow-up questions.

A Home Energy Score and report must exist before most publicly advertised Portland houses can be marketed. The score must appear in every ad, including the RMLS, online listings, yard signs and print, and the seller is ultimately responsible.

  • Coverage follows the City of Portland line and not the mailing address, and a few Portland addresses lie outside it.
  • An existing score and report can be reused for up to eight years if the home has not changed.
  • Manufactured, mobile and floating homes cannot be scored and are not required to have one.
  • An exemption can be requested by sellers in certain financial distress or with a condemned or uninhabitable house.
  • Sellers at or below 80 percent of Portland's area median income may be able to get a free score through Community Energy Project.

A sale that is not publicly advertised is not covered. The full rule is on the City of Portland Home Energy Score page.

sections.h2: Selling a house with a tenant
sections.html:
Ending a tenancy without cause, or declining to renew a fixed term, usually obliges the landlord to pay the tenant relocation assistance. Unit size decides the amount.

Unit sizeRelocation assistance
Studio or single room$2,900
1 bedroom$3,300
2 bedrooms$4,200
3 bedrooms or larger$4,500

The tenant must receive written notice no later than 90 days ahead, naming the amount owed. Skip the process and the exposure is up to three times the monthly rent, plus actual damages and attorney fees. One exemption covers a fixed-term tenancy where the tenant was told in advance that the home would be sold or permanently converted, and most exemptions need a filing with the Portland Housing Bureau.

Those costs lead some owners of occupied rentals toward a cash sale in which the tenant stays or the schedule is fixed in advance. The Portland Housing Bureau page and its helpdesk at 503-823-1303 can tell you how the rules fit your lease.

Portland homes get one Multnomah County bill that can be paid in three pieces, due November 16, February 16 and May 17 this tax year, 2026. The discount is 3 percent for the full amount and 2 percent for two-thirds. To keep the discount and avoid interest, the payment must arrive, or be postmarked, by the due date.

The county's Division of Assessment, Recording and Taxation mails the statements. Green means the owner pays directly; yellow means a mortgage company may pay on the owner's behalf. Real market value for 2026 was fixed as of January 1, 2026, and appeals close December 31, 2026.

Under Measures 5 and 50, the assessed value that drives the bill generally cannot climb more than about 3 percent a year. A house held for decades often carries an assessed value far below market, so what the buyer sees on your statement may not be what they end up paying. The county statement guide explains each part of the bill.

Each buyer who makes a written offer is owed a seller's property disclosure statement from most Oregon residential sellers. It asks about title, water, sewage, insulation, structure, systems, seismic and general conditions. After delivery the buyer holds five days to revoke, unless waived, and if you refuse to give the form, the buyer may revoke any time before closing.

A limited exclusion lets some sellers fill in Section 1 only. Excluded sales are a never-occupied dwelling sold for the first time, a foreclosing financial institution, a court-appointed personal representative, trustee, conservator or guardian, and a government agency. See ORS 105.464 and 105.470. A family selling an inherited house through an estate representative may fall in this group.

sections.h2: Your options as a Portland seller
sections.html:
Three paths: hire an agent, go it alone, or sell for cash. Each one balances time, cost and certainty in its own way.

  • A listing normally brings a Home Energy Score, photos, showings and haggling over repairs once the inspection is done.
  • Going alone spares you the listing-side commission, though marketing and paperwork become your job.
  • A cash deal is as-is, and you help pick the closing date.

Cash Home Buyers begins with a look at the property and a talk about your timing. Describe your Portland house and we will lay out what we can offer and what would be involved. You are never obliged to accept.

No lender is involved, so a loan appraisal and underwriting never enter the picture.

  1. Give us the address, an honest description of the house and the closing date you prefer.
  2. Study the written offer, paying attention to closing costs and any repairs left to you.
  3. Escrow opens through a title company, which looks for liens and unpaid taxes.
  4. You sign, the deed goes on record and your proceeds are paid out.

Back property tax comes out of what you receive at closing. A payoff figure from the title company, requested early, shows your real net before you commit. The settlement statement also divides the current tax year between seller and buyer.

• ID that matches the deed.
  • The latest tax statement, green or yellow.
  • Lender and loan number if a mortgage is being retired.
  • Any Home Energy Score report, if the house was scored.
  • Lease and notice records for an occupied rental.
  • Papers for permits, retrofits and drainage work.

faqs.q: Do I need a Home Energy Score to sell my Portland house?
faqs.a: Yes, when you advertise publicly inside the City of Portland, though manufactured homes and a few others are exempt. A private sale with no public advertising is not covered. A report can be reused for up to eight years if the home has not changed.

faqs.q: When are Portland property taxes due?
faqs.a: This tax year the three Multnomah County installments are due November 16, February 16 and May 17. A full payment on the first date takes 3 percent off, and two-thirds takes 2 percent off.

faqs.q: Do I owe my tenant money if I sell my Portland rental?
faqs.a: Possibly. Ending a tenancy without cause or not renewing a fixed term in Portland generally triggers relocation assistance of $2,900 to $4,500, depending on unit size, with 90 days written notice. Some exemptions exist, and most require a filing with the Portland Housing Bureau.

faqs.q: How much time does a buyer have to back out after the Oregon disclosure form?
faqs.a: Five days after the form is delivered, unless the buyer waived that right. A seller who withholds the form lets the buyer revoke right up to closing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Portland house with earthquake or landslide concerns?
faqs.a: Yes. Fill in the seismic questions truthfully, and a cash buyer will price the house as it stands. The 2014 mapping flagged over 7,000 high-risk locations.
